back: A question answered using data that varies. It names the variable, the group and the intent.
A characteristic that can change from one person or thing to the next, such as height or favourite sport.
A variable that puts each person or thing into a group or category, e.g. eye colour, postcode.
A variable that is a count or a measurement, e.g. number of pets, arm span in cm.

front: Is a rugby jersey number categorical or numerical?
back: Categorical: the number is just a label for a position.
Primary data you collect yourself. Secondary data was collected by someone else (e.g. Stats NZ, a website).
Data with more than two variables recorded for each person or thing.
Looks at one variable for one group, e.g. the typical arm span of Year 9 students.
Compares one variable across two groups, e.g. travel times of walkers vs bus users.
Looks for a link between two variables measured on the same people or things, e.g. height and arm span.
Looks at how one variable changes over time, e.g. school roll each year.
A study where you record things as they are, without changing anything (unlike an experiment).
